Hi Alyssa —

Thanks again for the call this morning. As discussed, before we lock a Dedicated configuration for the pilot I need two quick confirmations from you so we size the pool and draft the SOW correctly:

1) Model variant and expected context distribution — which of the two you expect to use most: the 32k finetuned variant (higher cache growth, slightly slower) or the 16k base variant (lower memory)? A short percent split (e.g., 70/30) helps.
2) Typical concurrent active requests at peak (not users; active in-flight gens) and desired p95 latency SLO.

Attached is the usage snapshot you shared (I pulled the session-level breakdown) — it has the token/session histogram. Once we have those two items Marcus will run a quick footprint matrix (KV cache growth, per-token memory, and quantization scenarios) and propose a small set of Dedicated pool options.

Tentatively we are looking at two pilot options we mentioned on the call:
- Option A: 4x A100-equivalent workers (higher memory per GPU) for the 32k variant, with int8 quantization to reclaim KB/slot.
- Option B: 8x A40-equivalent workers (more pods, smaller per-GPU memory) for the 16k variant, QAT or q4_0 quantization.

If procurement needs pricing/line-items early, say so and I’ll push a draft.

Thanks —
Hannah

Hi Hannah —

Thanks for the summary. Quick answers:

1) We expect to run the 32k finetuned variant for ~60% of traffic (customer-facing long-context analyses) and the 16k base variant for ~40% (internal tooling). The 32k usage spikes end-of-month but is otherwise steady.
2) Peak concurrent active requests: roughly 220 active gens (we measured number of in-flight calls during internal stress tests). Desired p95 latency is <= 800ms for customer flows; 1.5s is tolerable for internal.

Procurement: we need a cost worksheet with committed monthly units and an option for burst capacity. Timeline: we want an initial 6-week pilot starting mid-Oct and a production roll by mid-Nov if pilot looks good.

Subject: Re: Model footprint scenarios and KV/quant trade-offs for Novaprospect Dedicated

Hannah / Ben —

I ran three footprint scenarios based on Alyssa’s numbers (60/40 32k/16k; 220 concurrency peak; target p95 <= 800ms). Highlights below, full sheet attached (model-footprint-scenarios.xlsx). I included expected KV cache growth, per-GPU reserve for KV and model weights, and quantization delta.

Assumptions (conservative):
- 32k variant: base FP16 in-memory model weights ~40GB, KV cache growth ~2.4MB per active request per 1k tokens (we assume median response ~1k tokens for long jobs).
- 16k variant: weights ~28GB, KV growth ~1.3MB per active request per 1k tokens.
- Token/service overhead (batching buffers, framework): ~3GB per worker reserved.
- Quantization benefits: int8 -> ~35% model-weight memory reduction; q4_0 -> ~55% reduction with modest perf trade-offs. Offloading/kv-splitting reduces per-GPU KV memory but adds network/latency overhead.

Scenario A (fewer big GPUs, target 32k):
- 4 x A100-equivalent (80GB aggregate per-GPU config). After int8 quant and 10% headroom, each GPU can host ~1x 32k worker with KV headroom to support ~60 concurrent active requests across the pool before KV memory binds. That gets us to ~60 sustained concurrency on 32k jobs; to hit 220 we need either more workers or move KV to distributed offload.

Scenario B (more smaller GPUs, target mixed 16k/32k):
- 8 x A40/A5000-equivalent (48–48GB class). With q4_0 on 16k variants we can fit 1–2 workers per GPU for the 16k workload. The mixed workload at 220 concurrency requires ~10–12 pods if we keep KV in-GPU; with distributed KV offload we can reduce to ~8 pods but add ~50–120ms tail latency.

Key trade-offs and ops notes:
- If Novaprospect must keep p95 <= 800ms for 32k flows, distributed KV offload is risky unless we pin caching to local racks and use high-throughput NICs (RDMA preferred).
- Quantization unlocks rack-level capacity. q4_0 gives the biggest memory wins but requires a short validation pass — some tail-case failures in hallucination were seen on one customer with aggressive 4-bit quant; we can run a quick eval set during pilot.
- Autoscale sizing: provision baseline to cover 60% of expected peak (to honor committed throughput) and allow burst-roster to handle the remaining spike with pre-warmed pods to keep tail latency within SLO.

Recommendation (pilot):
- Start with Option B but with hybrid KV: keep KV in-GPU for 32k flows on 4 higher-memory pods and serve 16k via q4_0 on smaller pods. That gives a balance: 220 concurrency handled with expected p95 ~750ms in our perf sim, and a clear path to scale up pods if needed.

I attached the spreadsheet with the per-pod breakdown and cost delta. Happy to convert this into the SOW line-items (core count, reserved GPUs, monthly committed hours, burst policy).

—Marcus

Looping you in with the short recommendation from Marcus (below). Two action items if you’re good with the hybrid approach:

1) Confirm pilot scope: 6-week pilot starting week of Oct 13, Dedicated pool defined as: 4x high-memory pods (A100-equivalent) pinned for 32k in-GPU KV + 6x smaller pods (A40-equivalent) running q4_0 for 16k. Burst policy: +40% pre-warmed pods for end-of-month spikes.
2) We’ll deliver a draft SOW and a short validation plan (30 eval prompts to run against q4_0 / int8) by Friday.

Cost note: Marcus’ spreadsheet gives a projected committed unit ask of ~2,700 GPU-hours/month for the pilot configuration before burst; exact dollar line-items coming in the SOW draft.

If procurement needs a formal line-by-line cost now, we can produce that by EOD.

On the validation front, Marcus — can you own the q4_0 evaluation and the 30-prompt regression? Ben, can you prep the pilot onboarding checklist (network, RBAC, KMS)?
